main_text.p: mana oriatur & pendeat, errant toto cœ-lo. Nam animalis homo non percipit eâ quæ sunt Spiritus Dei: 1.Cor.2.14. uersa-tur in uanitate mentis suæ, cogitationem habens obscuratam & abalienatam à uita Dei, propter ignorantiam quæ est in eo ex obduratione cordis: Eph.4.17.18. Itaque nequaquam potest credere, quòd cę[?] ci sint oculi eius, & cor obduratum: Ioan. 12.39.40.

Sed si uoluntariam certitudinem esse dicit, quòd à Spiritu sancto mente illustrata, & uoluntate ad Deum conuersa, homo renatus sciens & uolens assentiatur promissioni gratiæ, & in ea acquiescat, libenter subscribemus. Spiritualis enim homo dijudicat, id est, intelligit ac discernit omnia: 1.Cor.2.15. Vult bonum facere, & delectatur Lege Dei secundum interiorem hominem: Rom.7.21.22.

3. Addit Definitor ille, Absentium. Fi-des, interveniente Spiritus sancti submi-nistratione, res absentes præsentes facit, & quodámodo sistit, sed pro diversa eâ-rum natura. Remissionem peccatorum & imputatione iustitiæ Christi, fides sic impetrat & applicat homini fideli, ut ad-

page.notes: The first word of the page is a fragment ("mana"); its opening letters are cut off at the edge, so it stays a fragment. The word before "sint" in "quòd cę[?] ci sint" is doubtful: the abbreviation with the cedilla is hard to read. The heading-like "Absentium." in the third paragraph is a running-text phrase as printed. The catchword "sint," is set at the lower right below the last line.
